lines.text: No right angle → sine rule if a side and its opposite angle are known; cosine rule for two sides and the angle between them, or three sides (3.2)
Sine rule for an angle, with “two possible values” or an obtuse angle → ambiguous case: test $\theta$ and $180^{\circ} - \theta$ (3.5)
Length or angle inside a 3D solid → find a right-angled triangle in it and draw that triangle on its own (3.1)
Arc, sector or segment → work in radians: $l = r\theta$, $A = \frac{1}{2}r^{2}\theta$, segment $=$ sector $-$ triangle (3.4)
Exact trig value of a larger angle → reference angle for the size, quadrant for the sign (3.5)
One ratio given, another wanted → Pythagorean identity for the size, quadrant for the sign (3.6)
Trig equation → sketch to count the solutions. For $2x$, change the interval first. A quadratic in $\sin x$ → factorise (3.8)

Angle between two vectors → $\cos\theta = \frac{\boldsymbol{v} \cdot \boldsymbol{w}}{\lvert\boldsymbol{v}\rvert\lvert\boldsymbol{w}\rvert}$. Between two lines, use their direction vectors and give the acute angle (3.13, 3.14)
Vector perpendicular to two vectors, a normal to a plane, or an area → vector product (3.16, 3.17)
Do two lines meet? → equate them with different parameters, solve two of the equations, test the third (3.15)
Where a line meets a plane → put the line's general point into the plane's equation and solve for $\lambda$ (3.18)
